version.purpose: Ensure every assessment (test, quiz, assignment or practical task) used to evaluate trainees measures the intended learning objectives fairly, accurately and consistently before it is issued.
version.scope: The assessment paper or brief, its item bank, answer key / model solutions, marking scheme, instructions and logistics. Excludes the delivery platform and the trainees' answers.
version.objective: An assessment is fit to issue when it scores 8 or above overall, with no factual errors in items or keys and no ambiguity that would let two competent trainees read a question differently.
version.guidance: Score each leaf from the rating matrix, not from overall impression. Count items where the quantitative guideline asks for a count or percentage. When evidence for the higher band is missing, choose the lower band. Metric leaves are scored from the measured values; override only with a written reason.

parameters.name: Purpose & Alignment
parameters.description: Does the assessment know what it is measuring, and does it measure exactly that?

children.name: Objective clarity
children.description: The learning objectives being assessed are stated explicitly and are measurable.

criteria.qualitative: Every objective is stated, measurable and uses an observable action verb; the audience and level are explicit.
criteria.quantitative: 100% of objectives use a measurable verb; 0 vague objectives ('understand', 'know')

criteria.qualitative: Objectives are explicit and measurable with one trivial wording issue.
criteria.quantitative: >= 95% measurable; at most 1 minor wording issue

criteria.qualitative: Objectives are explicit and mostly measurable; a reader knows what is being assessed.
Objectives are listed but some are generic; intent is still recoverable.
Objectives exist only as topic headings; measurability is weak.
Objectives must be inferred from the items; several readings possible.
criteria.quantitative: No explicit objective list; intent inferable for most items

criteria.qualitative: Objectives are unclear or contradict the items.
criteria.quantitative: No objective list; intent unclear for over a third of items

criteria.qualitative: No evident purpose; it is not possible to tell what is being assessed.
criteria.quantitative: No objectives and no recoverable intent

children.name: Objective coverage
children.description: Every stated objective is assessed by at least one item, in proportion to its importance.

metrics.name: Objectives covered by at least one item
metrics.description: Objectives mapped to one or more items / total objectives × 100

criteria.qualitative: Every objective is assessed, and item weighting matches objective importance.
Near-complete coverage with sensible weighting.
All key objectives covered; a minor objective is thin.
Most objectives covered; one notable objective missing.
Coverage is uneven; several objectives untested.
Large gaps between what is taught and what is tested.
Assessment tests a different subset from the stated objectives.
Assessment is largely unrelated to the objectives.

parameters.name: Item Quality
parameters.description: The individual questions / tasks are clear, correct and appropriately demanding.

children.name: Clarity & unambiguity
children.description: Each item has exactly one reasonable reading.

criteria.qualitative: Every item has exactly one reasonable reading; independent reviewers interpret all items identically.
All items clear; one cosmetic wording issue.
Items are clear; a small number need minor clarification that would not change answers.
criteria.quantitative: <= 2 items need minor clarification; none change the expected answer

criteria.qualitative: Mostly clear; one item could be answered differently by a careful reader.
Several items are open to interpretation.
Ambiguity is common; trainees would need to ask for clarification.
Frequent vague language; reviewers disagree on intent.
Items are statements of topic rather than questions; no clear task.

children.name: Technical correctness
children.description: Items, options, data and expected answers are factually and technically correct.

metrics.name: Factual / technical errors in items or keys
metrics.description: Count of items or answer-key entries containing a factual or technical error

criteria.qualitative: No errors in any item, option, data set or answer.
No errors, but one item relies on a version-specific or disputed fact without stating it.
One error that affects a single item.
One error that affects scoring of more than one item.
Two errors; trust in the assessment is reduced.
Errors in the answer key would mis-mark correct trainees.
criteria.quantitative: 2 errors, at least 1 in the key

criteria.qualitative: Multiple errors; the assessment cannot be used.

children.name: Cognitive rigour
children.description: The assessment demands the right depth of thinking for the level of the trainees.

children.name: Bloom's level distribution
children.description: Balance between recall and higher-order (apply, analyse, evaluate, create) items.

children.name: Higher-order item share
children.description: Share of marks on items at Bloom's 'Apply' level or above.

criteria.qualitative: Half or more of the marks require applying, analysing or creating.
Strong emphasis on application and analysis.
A healthy share of higher-order items.
Some higher-order items; recall dominates.
Higher-order items are token.
Very little application required.
Almost entirely recall.
Pure memorisation test.

children.name: Recall-only item share
children.description: Share of marks on items that only require remembering a fact (lower is better).

criteria.qualitative: Recall is used only where it is a prerequisite.
Recall is limited and purposeful.
Recall is present but balanced.
Recall is the majority of marks.
Recall dominates.
Recall heavily dominates.
Nearly all recall.
Recall only.

children.name: Difficulty calibration
children.description: Difficulty matches the trainees' level and discriminates between strong and weak performance.

criteria.qualitative: Deliberate difficulty ladder (easy → stretch) matched to the cohort; every item discriminates.
criteria.quantitative: Difficulty tagged for 100% of items; spread across >= 3 levels

criteria.qualitative: Well-calibrated ladder; one item slightly off-level.
Appropriate for the cohort with a clear easy-to-hard progression.
Generally appropriate; progression is implicit.
Noticeably too easy or too hard in places.
Mostly one difficulty level; little discrimination.
Mismatched to the cohort; most trainees would score similarly.
Difficulty bears no relation to the cohort.

parameters.name: Marking Scheme & Answer Key
parameters.description: Any two markers would give the same marks to the same response.

children.name: Answer-key completeness
children.description: Every item has an answer, model solution or acceptance criteria.

metrics.name: Items with an answer / model solution

criteria.qualitative: Every item has a complete answer or model solution, including acceptable alternatives.
Every item keyed; alternatives listed for most open items.
criteria.quantitative: 100% keyed; alternatives for >= 80% of open items

criteria.qualitative: Nearly every item keyed.
A few items lack keys.
Several items lack keys.
Key is partial.
Key is largely missing.
No usable key.

children.name: Marking objectivity
children.description: Mark allocation, partial credit and rubric descriptors leave no room for marker interpretation.

criteria.qualitative: Rubric specifies marks per step, partial credit and common wrong answers; any two markers agree.
criteria.quantitative: Marks per step for 100% of multi-step items; worked marking example provided

criteria.qualitative: Detailed rubric with partial-credit rules; no worked example.
criteria.quantitative: Marks per step for >= 90% of multi-step items

criteria.qualitative: Clear mark allocation and partial-credit guidance for most items.
Marks allocated per item; partial credit left to judgement.
Marks allocated per section only.
Total marks only; markers would diverge.
Marking is implied, not stated.
No marking scheme.

parameters.name: Fairness & Accessibility
parameters.description: Every trainee has an equal chance to demonstrate competence. Rolled up by MINIMUM: one unfair aspect makes the whole area unfair.

criteria.qualitative: Neutral, inclusive language and contexts throughout; reviewed for cultural assumptions.
criteria.quantitative: 0 items with biased or culture-specific context

criteria.qualitative: Inclusive throughout; one context could be more universal.
criteria.quantitative: 1 item with a mildly culture-specific context

criteria.qualitative: Neutral language; a couple of contexts assume local knowledge.
Some contexts advantage a subgroup.
Recurring assumptions about background knowledge.
Noticeable bias affecting outcomes.
Language that could offend or exclude.
Discriminatory content.
Instructions, allowed resources, time and submission format are explicit; timing validated by a dry run.
criteria.quantitative: All 4 elements stated; dry-run time within ±10%

criteria.qualitative: All elements explicit; timing estimated, not validated.
Instructions clear; one minor element implicit.
criteria.quantitative: 3 of 4 stated, missing one is minor

criteria.qualitative: Instructions adequate; time allowance is questionable.
Trainees would need to ask how to proceed.
Time is clearly insufficient or instructions contradictory.
Instructions largely missing.
No instructions.

children.name: Accessibility accommodations
children.description: Optional: mark N/A when the cohort has no declared accessibility needs.

criteria.qualitative: Accessible formats and accommodations are built in for all declared needs.
Accommodations available on request with a defined process.
Most needs accommodated informally.
Some needs accommodated.
Few needs accommodated.
Accommodations only after escalation.
Declared needs ignored.

children.name: Organisation & formatting
children.description: Logical ordering, consistent numbering, readable layout, marks shown per item.

criteria.qualitative: Sections ordered logically, consistent numbering and formatting, marks shown per item, no typos.
Professional layout with one cosmetic defect.
Clean and readable; a few cosmetic defects.
Readable; inconsistent numbering or formatting.
Disorganised in places; trainees may miss items.
Hard to follow.
Confusing structure; items out of order.
Unusable layout.
